claims.title: Damped drainage resolvent
claims.assumptions: C^(2,alpha) landscape; inward backward gradient flow; -Delta z >= kappa > 0; alpha L < kappa; positive Holder source
claims.conclusion: A positive bounded Holder b is constructed by an infinite characteristic integral; div(-b grad z)=rho globally in distributions.

claims.title: Critical-set criterion
claims.assumptions: Bounded smooth domain; zero boundary elevation and negative outward normal derivative; C^(2,alpha0) z; positive Holder rho; multiplier required bounded nonnegative continuous
claims.conclusion: A multiplier exists iff -Delta z is strictly positive at every critical point; constructed b is positive Holder and unique in the bounded continuous characteristic class. No claim for unbounded multipliers.

claims.title: General-domain weak-erosion steady existence
claims.assumptions: Bounded connected C^(2,alpha0) domain; zero elevation on the whole boundary; D>0; m,n>0; positive Holder U,rho; 0<=K<=K0
claims.conclusion: At least one classical-elevation conservative-flux steady state; z0/2<=z<=z0 and ||z-z0||_(2,alpha)<=C K. Neither elevation uniqueness nor arbitrary-K nonradial existence claimed.

claims.title: First-order small-erosion response
claims.assumptions: A family selected from Theorem thm:general
claims.conclusion: zK=z0-(K/D)P(b0^m |grad z0|^(m+n))+o(K), independent of branch selection at first order. The D=U=rho=1 case also gives the displayed first multiplier correction.

claims.title: Nonradial exact polynomial response check
claims.assumptions: Ellipse x^2/4+y^2<1; D=U=rho=1; m=n=1
claims.conclusion: Explicit z0,W,b1 satisfy the torsion and linear response equations exactly; z0-KW and 1+K b1 have residuals of order at least K^2, not zero at finite K.
computational_support: code/verify_global_bounds.py: exact-rational whole-square residual and positivity bounds for frozen decimal polynomials, not an exact-PDE enclosure

claims.title: All-parameter radial steady theorem
claims.assumptions: Ball B_R in dimension d>=1; constant U>0; rho=1; D,K>0; m,n>0; no point sources
claims.conclusion: Unique regular downhill radial steady state; a=r/d and q=x/d; positive slope bounded by U r/(dD); summit C^(2,gamma) regularity for gamma<min(1,m+n).

claims.title: Global monotone radial evolution and relaxation
claims.assumptions: Parameters as radial theorem, n>=1; nonincreasing radial C^(2,alpha) initial elevation with zero boundary value, regular center and displayed compatibility
claims.conclusion: Unique global classical positive-time radial evolution; a stationary larger-uplift slope bounds the gradient; |z-z*| <= C_in exp(-2dDt/R^2)(R^2-r^2). No nonradial or n<1 evolution assertion.

claims.location: Section 6; locate by result title in revised manuscript
claims.title: Universal profile with first correction
claims.assumptions: All m,n>0 and d>=1; p=m/n; positive radial universal profile

claims.title: Complete radial summit limit
claims.assumptions: D down to zero, other radial parameters fixed
claims.conclusion: Summit finite for p<1; logarithmically divergent with a finite renormalized constant for p=1; power divergence D^((n-m)/(m+n)) for p>1.

claims.location: Section 6; locate by result title in revised manuscript
claims.title: Scalar finite-summit viscosity limit
claims.assumptions: 0<p<1 in the radial small-diffusion limit
claims.conclusion: The finite cusp limit is a continuous viscosity solution of the scalar limiting stream-power Hamilton-Jacobi equation on the whole ball. This is not a BDN system viscosity theorem.

claims.title: All weighted relief moment thresholds
claims.assumptions: beta>0; radial parameters fixed as D down to zero
claims.conclusion: V_beta has finite/log/power regimes at p=beta+1. In dimension d total volume has threshold p=d+1. Supercritical D exponent is [n(beta+1)-m]/(m+n).

claims.title: Unique slope maximum
claims.assumptions: All positive radial exponents
claims.conclusion: The universal slope has exactly one nondegenerate maximum. The physical maximum is at ell*rho_star when that point lies inside the ball.

claims.title: Integrable radial family and constants
claims.assumptions: d>1 and m=n(d-1)
claims.conclusion: w satisfies dw/dtau=1-w^n; explicit exponential and hyperbolic-tangent cases at n=1,2; gamma-function integrals and logarithmic constants.

claims.title: No sink-free compact sublevel basin
claims.assumptions: C1 topography; compact internal sublevel basin; positive rainfall; nonnegative downhill contributing area; no sink allowed
claims.conclusion: A nonnegative test function yields a contradiction to div q=rho.

claims.title: Full-system planar wet-dry traveling fronts
claims.assumptions: Affine bed on unbounded space; h=alpha(x.nu-Vt)_+; zero rainfall; positive coefficients/exponents; v_w=-(b+alpha nu); V=v_w.nu
claims.conclusion: The displayed h,z,c solve all three conservative equations distributionally; water h satisfies the scalar viscosity inequalities at the front. Classified within the one-sided traveling affine-bed ansatz, not arbitrary data.

claims.title: Global wet-up from full vacuum
claims.assumptions: Spatially homogeneous continuous nonnegative rainfall; affine bed plus time-dependent offset; h(0)=0; m,n>0
claims.conclusion: Unique solution within this ansatz using the displayed Volterra formula for hc; 0<=c<=constant*h^m; includes elementary constant-rainfall family. Not a finite-energy general-domain theorem.

claims.title: Contradictory printed profile normalization
claims.assumptions: Printed 2008 page 1673 ODE, support/no-flux conditions, c_star>0 and integral w=c_star
claims.conclusion: Integrating gives integral w - (m-1)^(-1) integral w^(1/m)=c_star, so the additional printed normalization is impossible for a nonzero nonnegative profile.

claims.title: Complete corrected positive profile problem
claims.assumptions: m>1; c_star>0; w positive on [0,L); w_prime(0)=0; w(L)=0 and zero after L; omit the incompatible integral normalization
claims.conclusion: Unique amplitude from V(A)=c_star^2/2 and unique energy-quadrature profile; corrected integral identity; width strictly decreases with c_star and pi/2<L<pi*m/(m-1), with sharp endpoint limits.
computational_support: code/verify_structural.py: nine quadrature cases and zero-flux profile identity

claims.title: Separable time-factor correction
claims.assumptions: The corrected profile and u=(T-t)^(-1/(m-1))w^(1/m)
claims.conclusion: Dirac coefficient is c_star*(T-t)^(-m/(m-1)), not a fixed positive constant. This is a timed-sink blow-up family, not the conjectured fixed-coefficient problem.

claims.title: Correct zero-extension and moving-boundary flux identity
claims.assumptions: Regular moving interface, continuous u=0 at its edge, finite trace of (u^m)_x and locally integrable zero-extended u_t
claims.conclusion: q=C(t)-N_prime(t), where C(t)=integral u^m and N(t)=integral u. Fixed Dirac coefficient C together with integral u^m=C forces N_prime=0 in this class. No exclusion of more singular formulations.

claims.title: Variable-coefficient rescaling audit
claims.assumptions: Smooth amplitude/dilation/time transformation u=A(t)V(B(t)x,tau(t))
claims.conclusion: Normalizing diffusion, reaction and fixed sink imposes B^2=lambda and A^m B=1, while nonconstant scales generally retain amplitude and dilation terms. Not a theorem ruling out every possible transform.

claims.title: Eigenfunction-weighted radial contraction
claims.assumptions: Same parameters, monotone radial compatible initial data, m>0 and n>=1
claims.conclusion: Weighted sup distance contracts at exp(-D lambda_1 t); stronger relaxation with a different initial norm. Radial only.

claims.title: Second radial outer correction
claims.conclusion: rho^p y=1+A1 rho^(-q)+A2 rho^(-2q)+O(rho^(-3q)); c=0 has exponential correction
computational_support: code/verify_extensions.py: coefficient identities; first-correction sampling; second numerical coefficient diagnostic only

claims.title: Finite-moment correction threshold
claims.assumptions: beta>0; p<beta+1; fixed parameters as D decreases
claims.conclusion: Correction regimes separated by beta=2p; coefficients may vanish, no universally sharp leading rate claimed

claims.title: Constructive local nonradial uniqueness
claims.assumptions: Constant D,U,rho>0; m,n>0; m+n>=1; C2alpha domain; global Lip(grad z0)<U/D; sufficiently small K; bounded nonnegative continuous multiplier; elevation in the specified C2alpha ball
claims.conclusion: Unique local branch, nested contraction, multiplier Lipschitz bound and parameter stability. All ellipsoids d>=2 meet the geometric margin; no arbitrary-K or arbitrary-flux uniqueness.
computational_support: code/verify_nonradial.py: illustrative finite-grid collocation, not a certificate of the theorem

claims.title: Continuum a posteriori bounds
claims.assumptions: Invariant ball and multiplier interval; exact continuum residual norms; contraction constants eta,Q<1
claims.conclusion: Explicit elevation and multiplier error bounds from inner and outer residuals. Finite-grid PDE residuals do not supply these norms.

claims.title: Constraint derivative and necessary width
claims.assumptions: m>1; finite positive C1 moving boundary on compact positive-time intervals; pulled-back V continuous in time into C1 and W1,1 in time into L1; stated interior chain rule; uniform integrable domination of V^a V_yy and V^(-1/m)|V_y|^2; boundary traces as displayed; weaker conditional classes yield only the a.e. identity unless continuity is known.
claims.conclusion: The sufficient class gives C1 positive-time mass and the constraint derivative. Preserving integral u^m selects a Rayleigh quotient for lambda. Lambda=1 gives f>=pi sqrt(m(m-1))/(2m-1), strictly for positive edge flux. No existence theorem for the nonlocal model.

claims.title: Compact-data compatibility obstruction
claims.assumptions: m>1; C>0; explicit small positive compact cosine perturbation; right derivative identity at t=0, ensured for example by the stated fixed-domain time continuity, absolute continuity and uniform domination extending to zero with f(0)>0. Spatial integrability of initial data alone is insufficient.
claims.conclusion: Initial mass and edge flux both equal C but the constraint derivative is positive, excluding a constraint-preserving evolution in that regularity class. Does not refute the strictly positive infinite-support conjecture.
computational_support: code/verify_compatibility.py: exact identities and sampled quadratures with analytical remainder budget

claims.title: Consolidated sufficient smallness constants
claims.assumptions: Constants and invariant C2,alpha ball of thm:localunique fixed first; global Lipschitz L<lambda; Schauder and C0-to-C1 Poisson constants available.
claims.conclusion: An explicit minimum of symbolic positive bounds ensures multiplier interval invariance, inner Lipschitz contraction, elevation ball invariance and Q<=1/2. Constants are not numerically instantiated; ellipse torsion ratios 4/5 and 1/5 check only the geometric margin.

claims.title: Inexact nested iteration with finite inner stopping
claims.assumptions: Fixed admissible tau>0; eta,Q<1; every approximate elevation in the invariant C2,alpha ball; interval-preserving inner evaluations with continuum error delta_j<=(1-eta)r_j/4 at evaluated iterates; continuum Poisson error pi_j.
claims.conclusion: Starting from b_circ, the inner step criterion <=r_j terminates after finitely many steps. Exact residual <=r_j+delta_j gives E_(j+1)<=Q E_j+xi_j and its convolution bound. Geometric error budgets converge. Flow, quadrature, infinite-tail and Poisson errors remain separate; no implemented certified numerical algorithm is claimed.
